Mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC) <125mm or oedema caseload, as a % of the 6-59 months old population, Niger
rows.explainer: ALIMA estimates that total malnutrition caseload in Niger of children presenting with mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC) <125mm and/or oedema is equivalent to 33-35% of children aged 6-59 months. We discount this somewhat because we have tested the assumption of 33-35%, and it implies MAM coverage >50%, which is substantially higher than what ALIMA would guess (20-35%).

SAM cases (defined as MUAC<115mm or oedema) as a % of total cases treated
rows.explainer: ALIMA estimates that the ratio of SAM cases (defined as MUAC <115mm or oedema) to all cases of MUAC <125mm or oedema will be approximately 35-37% in the first year of programming, and will decline to 25% given strong MAM coverage (i.e., fewer kids developing SAM because of higher levels of MAM treatment). Based on these estimates, we assume a linear decline in the ratio from 37% in 2022 to 25% in 2026.

rows.explainer: GiveWell reports this model's result in multiples of cash transfers. Multiplying by GiveWell's value of a dollar to GiveDirectly converts it into units of value per dollar, so it ranks against the other models. Older sheets used older moral weights; the multiple of cash is the comparable number across years.
